Proceedings:- Mr. King S. Kum appeared for the Police.
Mr. Sung Tung for the 1st accused.
Mr. Lieu Yoong Koh for the 4th accused.
Mr. Liang Pah Hwa appointed for the 2nd and 3rd accused.

Mr. Kum:- The accused are charged under Articles 2
and 6 of the Laws Governing the punishment of Persons who Commit
acts with intent to injure the Republic of China. At 11.35.am.,
1.5.1933, S.P.C.682 was on duty on Peking Road, when he saw the 1st
and 2nd accused followed by a crowd of about forty people walking
along Peking Road from West to East and distributing pamphlets.
S.P.C.682 arrested the 2nd accused and gave instructions to S.P.C.
197 to arrest the 1st accused, and the 3rd and 4th accused were ar-
rested by S.P.C.664 whilst they were walking along Peking Road near
Chekiang Road. These pamphlets (produced) were found on the
ground, and they are of a Communistic nature. Nothing of an incrim-
inating nature was found in the 2nd, 3rd and 4th accused' possession,
but when the Police raided the house of the 1st accused they found
a quantity of Communistic Books in Chinese and English. The 1st of
May is a Communist anniversary and they were holding a meeting
and demonstrating on the road.

Continental Building for tiffin. With regard to the books found

D.S.Logan:- I stated at the last hearing that after
their arrest I made enquiries and the 1st accused led us to No.310
Avenue Road, where we found these books (produced), which he said
belonged to his friend who had gone to Canton. There is a list of
the books in Chinese before the Court.

2nd accused:- I was arrested at 11.30.am., 1.5.1933,
on Peking Road when I was walking from West to East on my way home.
I did not have any pamphlets or banners in my possession and I did
not shout any slogans. I was not the leader of the crowd. I have
been employed in a foodshop on Nansen Road, Yangtsepoo, for three
years, and the day in question I asked a substitute to do my work
whilst I had a day's holiday. I am not a Communist and I did not
take part in the Peoples Self Salvation Association.

3rd accused:- I was arrested on Peking Road near
Thibet Road and near the Anglo-Chinese Dispensary on the 1.5.1933.
I did not distribute pamphlets or shout slogans. I heard a crowd
shouting and some of them were throwing pamphlets and there were
many pedestrians standing watching, but when the Police came on the
scene they scattered. I was also watching and then I was arrested.
I did not know that it was a Communist anniversary on that day. I
am not a Communist and on that day I was going to Nantao to borrow
some money.

4th accused:- I had just finished my tiffin in a
foodshop and when I left the place I saw a quantity of pamphlets on
the ground. I am employed in the Chung Hwa Printing Company on
Thibet Road, and I was going back to the shop to work after having
finished my tiffin. I did not have any banners in my possession.

REPORT
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE C. & S. B. REGISTRY. Special Branch D. 4801/2 Date: May 13 1933）

Subject (in full) Further inquiries in connection with addressed letter found
in the room of the accused Han Lien Ts (韓連子).
Made by D.S. Tilton Forwarded by D.S. Tilton 01.

In connection with the addressed letter found in
the room of the accused Han Lien Ts, a further statement was
taken down and signed by him on May 13. He adheres to his
former explanation that this letter which was written by him
is only a friendly one, and the persons mentioned therein are
not interested in politics or members of any society. From
the interrogation of the accused on the morning of May 12, and
from his vague answer to questions relating to persons
mentioned in the letter, it is suspected that the person
previously mentioned by the accused as Wong Jih Hwa (王日華)
whom he declares is the owner of the pro-Communistic books
in French, German, English and Japanese, is an imaginary
person invented by the accused to cover the ownership of
the books, and the books are possibly owned by either Zung
Joo Ling, 张武岗 or Ying Poo (盈波), former visitors to
Shanghai, and both of whom are stated by the accused to
be in Tokio.

Translation of the letter is attached, together
with the statement of the accused.

D. S. Tilton
D. S.
Officer i/c Special Branch.

D.S. Tilton.

Translation of a letter
Envelope addressed to:-
Zung Woo Ling (陈武陵),
Chinese Y.M.C.A. in Japan,
No.10 Kitajinpocho, Kandaku,
Tokio, Japan.
From Han (韩), Shanghai.
--------------------------

Mr. Woo Ling,
Your letter has been noted. You ask me
to return your manuscript but it has been sent by Kai
Sien (闻先) to Tokio together with Ying Poo's (盈波)
manuscript. Therefore you can ask Ying Poo direct.
This is the first time, but you grumble
very much without reasonable cause. I believe it is
due to your being too suspicious of others.
I shall be glad to receive your letters
from time to time. I just dismiss your mock with
a smile. In a word, why need you 'square up your
accounts' with Ying Poo?
Looking from a-far I see that Japan is
full of cloud. Take good care of your health.

Han Tsai Yuan (韩菜園).
pages.zh:
信件译文
信封收件人：-
陈武陵（Zung Woo Ling），
日本基督教青年会，
日本东京神田区北神保町10号。
寄件人：韩（Han），上海。
--------------------------

武陵先生：
来信已悉。你要求我
归还你的手稿，但该手稿已由开先（Kai
Sien）连同盈波（Ying Poo）的手稿一并寄往
东京。因此你可以直接向盈波索取。
这是第一次，但你却毫无理由地
抱怨甚多。我相信这是由于你对他人
过于猜疑所致。
我很高兴不时收到你的来信。对于你的
嘲弄，我只是一笑置之。总之，你何必与
盈波“算清账目”呢？
遥望日本，乌云密布。请保重
身体。

韩菜园（Han Tsai Yuan）。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.

REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Han Lien Ts.
native of Kwangtung. taken by me D.S. Tilton.
at Police Hdqrs on the 12.5.33. and interpreted by Clerk Fang Kuo Liang.

In connection with the letter addressed to Zung
Woo Ling (陳武陵), Chinese Y.M.C.A. in Japan, No.10
Kitajinpocho, Kandaku, Tokio, Japan, which was found in my
room at 310 Avenue Road, I have to explain that Zung Woo
Ling is aged about 30 years and a fellow countryman. I met
him about four years ago in Shanghai. He is a student and
left Shanghai for Tokio about two years ago to continue his
studies. I do not know the college in Tokio which he attends.
I last heard from him about one year ago, when he mentioned
that he intended to take a course of bookkeeping. I believe
that he can speak Japanese. The letter found in my room was
in answer to his letter which I believe I received in November
1932. The person mentioned in my letter as Ying Poo (盈波)
is also in Tokio. I do not know his address, but the other
person mentioned in the letter as Kai Sien (開先) is
acquainted with these facts. Kai Sien is also a student,
now attending the China Public School, Avenue Foch, French
Concession.

Zung Woo Ling and Ying Poo are old friends and are
now companions in Tokio. The letter is only a friendly one
and really refers to two manuscripts written respectively by
Zung Woo Ling and Ying Poo, both manuscripts on stories of
love and romance. Zung Woo Ling sent both manuscripts to
me through Kai Sien, to criticize and to endeavour to sell
to a publisher. I returned both manuscripts to Kai Sien and
informed him in my opinion Zung's story was inferior. Kai
Sien returned both manuscripts to the authors, Zung and Ying,

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL C. S. B. REGISTER File No. V. D # 801/2）

Subject (in full) Further information in connection with Han Lien Ts (韓連三) and lists of documents and addresses found in his room at No. 310 Avenue Road.
Made by D.S. Tilton Forwarded by O.B.Ru. Q.I.

At 2.30 p.m. May 3 the chief tenant named Zung Li Sz (陳李氏) of No. 310 Avenue Road was brought to the office together with the 1st accused Han Lien Ts for further interrogation, and as a result of same, further statements were taken down as attached.

The 1st accused admits that he is at present acting as the general secretary of the "Soviet Research Society" which he declares was promoted by Zung Ping Woo (陳彬龢), an editor of the Shun Pao newspaper, Sun Ts Tsaung (沈志章), a departmental chief of the Chinese Y.M.C.A., French Concession, Zau Liang (曹亮), assistant dean of the Medhurst College, Chaoufoong Road, Woo Yu Ts (胡愈之), formerly the editor of the "Eastern Miscellany Magazine", and others unknown to him. This society is not registered with the Municipality of Greater Shanghai and was inaugurated in the Chinese Y.M.C.A., French Concession, during January 1933, where he declares meetings were held, but he was not present. The documents relating to this society found in his room were left there by Zau Liang, a member of the "Executive Committee", under whom the 1st accused was working.

A list of the names and addresses of the members of the above committee were found with the documents seized, copies of which are attached to this report together with lists of addresses which the accused declares are his relations, friends and acquaintances.

With reference to the pro-communist books found in his room, the accused adheres to his former statement that same were left by his former friend, one named Wong Jih Hwa (王日華), aged 27, native of Kwangtung, who was educated in Japan, and returned to his native home about July 1932. The accused declares that

5月3日下午2时30分，爱文义路310号的主要租户陈李氏（Zung Li Sz）与第一被告韩连三一同被带到办公室接受进一步讯问，结果如下，所附为补充供词。

第一被告承认，他目前担任“苏俄研究会”的总干事，他声称该会由《申报》编辑陈彬龢（Zung Ping Woo）、法租界中华基督教青年会部门主管沈志章（Sun Ts Tsaung）、兆丰路麦赫斯特学院（Medhurst College）副院长曹亮（Zau Liang）、前《东方杂志》编辑胡愈之（Woo Yu Ts）以及其他他不认识的人发起。该社团未在大上海市政府注册，并于1933年1月在法租界中华基督教青年会成立，他声称会议在此举行，但他并未出席。在他房间内发现的与该社团有关的文件是由“执行委员会”成员曹亮留下的，第一被告曾在其手下工作。

在查获的文件中发现了一份上述委员会成员的姓名和地址清单，其副本连同被告声称是其亲属、朋友和熟人的地址清单一起附在本报告后。

D.S. Tilton
Section 2,3.B. May 3, 1933. Clerk Zung.

The Soviet Research Society was promoted by the following persons:-
Zung Ping Woo(陳彬龢), an editor of the Shun Pao Newspaper.
Sun Ts Tsang(沈志華), a departmental chief of the Chinese
Y.M.C.A. in French Concession.
Zau Liang (曹良), assistant dean of the Medhurst College,
Chaoufoong Road.
Woo Yu Ts (胡愈之), formerly editor of the "Eastern
Miscellany" magazine, published by the Commercial Press.
and others unknown to me, but whose names appear on a document
found in my room.
I was appointed to work under Zau Liang as a general
secretary from early in February at a monthly salary of $10.00
which was paid to me by Zau Liang. This society is
about to apply for registration with the Municipality of
Greater Shanghai. It was inaugurated in the Chinese Y.M.C.A.
in French Concession about January, 1933, where the meetings
are held.
The documents relating to this society found in my room
were left there by Zau Liang pending the registration of the
society, when an office will be opened.
The names and addresses found in the room on letters,
papers, and envelopes are of my relatives, friends and
acquaintances.
Wang Jih Hua(王日華), aged 27, whom I mentioned in my
first statement, returned home to Kwangtung about ten months
ago. He was educated in Japan and can speak, read and

苏联研究会由以下人士发起：-
Zung Ping Woo (陳彬龢)，《申报》编辑。

Woo Yu Ts (胡愈之)，前商务印书馆出版的《东方杂志》编辑。
以及其他我不认识的人，但他们的名字出现在我房间里发现的一份文件上。
我从二月初开始被任命在 Zau Liang 手下担任总秘书，月薪10.00美元，由 Zau Liang 支付给我。该社团正准备向大上海市政府申请注册。它于1933年1月左右在法租界中华基督教青年会成立，会议也在那里举行。
在我房间里发现的与该社团有关的文件是 Zau Liang 留下的，等待社团注册后开设办公室时使用。
在房间里的信件、纸张和信封上发现的姓名和地址是我的亲戚、朋友和熟人。
我在第一次供词中提到的 Wang Jih Hua (王日華)，27岁，大约十个月前回广东老家了。他在日本受过教育，能说、读和

write Japanese, English, and he is also a fair German
scholar. He studied in Japan about three years ago
and returned to China during 1931. He is a very old
friend of mine, and I met him in Shanghai about eleven
months ago. The pro-communist books found in my room
were given to me by him when he left Shanghai. He stated
he would write to me and claim his books when he returns
to Shanghai, but I have not heard from him.

(Signed) Han Lieu Ts.

写日语、英语，他的德语水平也不错。他大约三年前在日本学习，并于1931年回到中国。他是我的老朋友，我大约十一个月前在上海遇到他。在我房间里发现的亲共书籍是他离开上海时给我的。他说他回到上海后会写信给我并取回他的书，但我一直没有收到他的消息。

（签名）Han Lieu Ts。

Zung Li Sz (陈李氏)
Lo Tien, Kiangsu                                D.S. Tilton
Headquarters        May 3, 1933,                Clerk Fung Kuo Liang

My name is Zung Li Sz, aged 52, native of Lo Tien
(罗店), Kiangsu, residing at No.310 Avenue Road.    The
accused Han Lien Ts (韩连之) came alone to the house and
rented an upstairs room on April 1 at monthly rent of $9.00
which he paid in advance.  I did not observe how his
trunks and personal effects were brought to the house,
as some were taken through the rear door.
    I did not pay any particular attention to his
subsequent movements, and I did not see him receive any
visitors.  He told me that he was employed as a clerk
in a firm, and habitually returned home early every evening
and did not keep late hours.  I noticed however that he
received a number of letters by post.

                                    (Signed)  Zung Li Sz.

江苏罗店                                D.S. Tilton
总部        1933年5月3日，                书记员 Fung Kuo Liang

我叫 Zung Li Sz，52岁，江苏罗店人，居住在爱文义路310号。被告 Han Lien Ts (韩连之) 独自来到这所房子，于4月1日租了一间楼上的房间，月租金9.00美元，他预付了租金。我没有注意到他的行李箱和个人物品是如何搬进房子的，因为有些是从后门搬进去的。
    我没有特别关注他随后的行动，也没有看到他接待任何访客。他告诉我他在一家公司当职员，习惯每天晚上很早回家，不熬夜。不过，我注意到他收到了许多邮政信件。

                                    （签名） Zung Li Sz。

Charge
Charge against 1st, 2nd, 3rd, & 4th accused:-
Breach of the Law governing the punishment of persons who commit
acts with intent to injure the Republic of China, Cent. to Art.
2 Sub Section 2 and Art. 6 also Art. 103 of the C.C.R.C.
For that they conspired together at about 11.30 a.m. 1.5.33.
on Peking Road, did distribute certain literature of a rebellious
nature with intent to subvert the constitution of the Republic of
China and which was irreconcilable with the "Three Peoples"
Principles.

For Proceedings of the 5th accused. See Sheet No. 2.

HIGH COURT A.M.

Proceedings. Messrs Kun and Lee appeared for the Police.

Mr Lee:- The 1st, 2nd, 3rd, and 4th accused in this are char-
ged under Art's. 2. and 6. of the Law governing the punishment of per-
sons who commit acts with intent to injure the Republic of China,
and also Art. 103. of the C.C.R.C. At about 11.30.a.m. on the 1/5/33,
the 1st and 2nd accused were walking from West to East on the Peking
Road, distributing pamphlets and being followed by about forty per-
sons. The incident was witnessed by S.P.C. 662. who arrested the 2nd
accused, the 1st accused was later arrested by S.P.C. 177. The 3rd
and 4th accused were arrested by S.P.C. 664. When the 1st accused was
questioned at the Police Station he stated that he was living at No.
510. Avenue Road, and when this address was raided by the police sev-
eral books of a communistic nature was seized. The 1st accused stat-
ed that the books were the property of a friend. The 2nd accused st-
ated that he was employed in the T'Poo District and that he took the
day off with the intention of participating in this meeting. The 5th
accused was arrested on the Tibet Road in possession of a flag and
the police make an application to the court that he be detained on
writ of detention for the purpose of further enquiry.

指控
对第1、2、3及4名被告的指控：-
违反《危害民国紧急治罪法》，依据该法第二条第二款及第六条，以及《中华民国刑法》第一百零三条。
因为他们于1933年5月1日上午11时30分左右在北京路共谋分发某些具有叛逆性质的文献，意图颠覆中华民国宪法，且这些文献与“三民主义”原则不相容。

关于第5名被告的诉讼程序，见第2页。

S.P.C.682:- At 11.55.a.m. on the 1/5/33, I saw the 1st and the 2nd accused walking from West to East on Peking at the same time throwing pamphlets. I called the assistance of S.P.C.197, who arrested the 2nd accused and I arrested the 1st accused. They were taken to the Police Station together with the pamphlets which gathered from the roadway.

S.P.C.197:- At about 11.55.a.m. on the 1/5/33, I was on duty on Peking Road near Kwechow Road, where I was called upon to stop the accused who were proceeding from West to East throwing pamphlets. I succeeded in arresting the 2nd accused.

S.P.C.664:- At about 11.30. am. on the 1/5/33, I was on duty on Peking Road near Chefoo Road, where my attention was drawn to a crowd of chinese men who were throwing pamphlets. I arrested the 3rd and 4th accused, the others dispersed.

指控：根据《中华民国刑事诉讼法》第六章申请拘留令。
工部局警务处特此申请拘留上述人员，该人于1933年5月1日上午11时40分在西藏路被捕，涉嫌为从事共产主义活动的团体成员，以便进一步查问。

警员682号：1933年5月1日上午11时55分，我看见第一和第二被告在北京路上由西向东行走，同时散发传单。我呼叫警员197号协助，他逮捕了第二被告，我逮捕了第一被告。他们连同从路面上收集的传单一起被带往警察局。

警员197号：1933年5月1日上午11时55分左右，我在靠近贵州路的北京路上执勤，当时我被叫去拦截那些由西向东行走并散发传单的被告。我成功逮捕了第二被告。

警员664号：1933年5月1日上午11时30分左右，我在靠近芝罘路的北京路上执勤，此时我的注意力被一群正在散发传单的华人男子所吸引。我逮捕了第三和第四被告，其余人四散而去。

副督察 Logan：在五名被告被捕后，我进行了查问。第一被告称其居住在爱文义路319号，对该地址楼上后间的一间小房间进行搜查后，查获了用英文、法文和日文写成的共产主义书籍，还查获了其他具有共产主义性质的书籍以及大量文件和信件。第二被告称其在胶州路670号受雇担任厨师，经在该地址查问，证实其陈述属实，且他已在该处受雇三年。昨日他找人替班，其雇主称他于上午7时离开，并未说明请假原因。

At about 11.35 a.m.1-5-33,S.P.C.682 saw the 1st and
2nd accused walking West to East on Peking Road,
throwing pamphlets to a crowd of about forty persons
who were following behind them,clapping their hands
and shouting loudly. S.P.C.682 succeeded in arresting
the 2nd accused and in calling upon S.P.C.197 to
arrest the 1st accused. S.P.C.197 thereupon effected
the arrest of the 1st accused, but did not see him
throwing any pamphlets. About 100 yards west of the
above described place, that is, at Chefoo & Peking
Roads corner, S.P.C.664 saw the 3rd and 4th accused
walking in front of a considerable crowd of people
to whom they were both distributing pamphlets, and
arrested them. At the time of arrest none of the
four accused had any pamphlets in his possession as
the pamphlets were discarded on the arrival of the
Police, but large quantities of pamphlets were
strewn on the roadway;these were collected, and
classified as per list attached hereto. When the
accused were brought to the Station,D.I.Ross attached
to the Special Branch was present and he detailed
D.S.Tilton and Clerk Fang Koh Liang to assist with
enquiries.

自约一年前以来一直是该地址食品店的店主，还证实他的生意状况极差，且他于同日早上7时离家，目的是去市区拜访一位朋友，希望向其借钱。当被问及他在上午7时至上午11时35分被捕期间做了什么时，他称他去了东余杭路514号他哥哥的店铺，在那里喝了一杯茶并等待了约一小时。当被问及该地址是否有人能证实他的陈述时，他说没有人看见他去那里，他也没有见到里面的任何人。鉴于其陈述明显虚假，未朝该方向进行查问。第四被告的家和工作场所均被查访，但未发现任何罪证。四名被告已被起诉。
将申请延期审理，以便对其背景进行进一步查问。

pages.en:
Han Lien Ts (          )
Kwangtung                                D.S. Tilton
Louza Station      May 1, 1933,          Clerk Yang Tho Liang

My name is Han Lien Ts, age 28, married, native of
Wen Cheng Hsien (          ), Kwangtung. At the age of 8, I
began my studies in a primary school in my native village,
having finished both the preliminary and high course at the
age of 17. I then entered the Middle School of No.6 Normal
School also in the native village, graduating from this
institution at the age of 21, when I studied at the Kwangtung
University at Canton. I left the university without graduating
in January 1930. In March I came to Shanghai to study
English preparing to go abroad to continue my education, but
I did not owing to lack of funds.
On arrival here I lived at No.1 Wen Nien Fang (          ),
Huang Pang Road, Chapoi. On January 30, 1932, two days after
the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese hostilities, I removed from
Chapoi to No.565 Dah Bang Yau-ng (          ), Hart Road. Three
months later I removed to No.30 San Nyi Fang (          ), Jessfield
Road, from where, after renting for three months, I removed
to a house in Heng Kong Li (          ), Chengtu Road. I have
occupied my present address, 310 Avenue Road, since March 1,
1933.
I cannot find a job in Shanghai so I support myself
by contributing articles to newspapers, magazines, etc., by
which I earn an average sum of $20 a month. In addition I
receive money ranging from $60 to $100 in every two months
from my uncle at Bangkok, Siam.
At 11 a.m. to-day I left my home and proceeded to the
Chung Fah Dispensary, at the corner of Peking and Chafee Roads,
pages.zh:
韩连茨 (          )
广东                                D.S. Tilton
老闸捕房      1933年5月1日，          书记员 杨托良

本人姓名韩连茨，28岁，已婚，籍贯广东文昌县 (          )。8岁时，我在本村小学开始读书，17岁时修完初等和高等课程。随后我进入同样位于本村的第六师范学校中学部就读，21岁从该校毕业，之后在广州的广东大学求学。1930年1月，我在未毕业的情况下离开大学。3月，我来到上海学习英语，准备出国继续深造，但因资金不足未能成行。
抵达上海后，我居住在闸北黄庞路文念坊1号 (          )。1932年1月30日，即中日战事爆发两天后，我从闸北搬至哈特路大邦里565号 (          )。三个月后，我搬至极司菲尔路三义坊30号 (          )，在此租住三个月后，又搬至成都路恒康里 (          ) 的一处房屋。自1933年3月1日起，我一直居住在现址爱文义路310号。
我在上海找不到工作，因此靠向报纸、杂志等投稿维持生计，平均每月收入20元。此外，每两个月我还能收到暹罗曼谷叔叔寄来的60至100元不等的汇款。
今天上午11点，我离家前往北京路与芝菲路转角处的中华诊疗所，

pages.en:
- 2 -

where I purchased a tooth brush and a packet of tooth cream.
I left the dispensary and when I was walking near Peking
Theatre on Peking Road near Kweichow Road, an Indian policeman
approached me and, mistaking the purchases I made at the
dispensary as pamphlets, he stopped me and took me into custody.

In addition to the above, I also earn a salary of
$15 per mensem for managing the affairs of the Soviet Union
Research Society.

With reference to the pro-communistic books in
Chinese, English, French and Japanese, found in my room, they
are left by one of my friends named Wong Jih Hua (    ),
native of Kwangtung, who returned to his native place in Spring
last year.

I can read and speak English a little but I cannot
write. I cannot read nor write nor speak Japanese.

(Signed)   Nam Lien Ta.
pages.zh:
- 2 -

在那里购买了一把牙刷和一包牙膏。离开诊疗所后，当我走到靠近贵州路的北京路北京大戏院附近时，一名印度巡捕走近我，误将我在诊疗所购买的物品当作传单，于是拦住我并将我拘留。

除上述收入外，我还因管理苏联研究会的事务，每月领取15元薪水。

关于在我房间内发现的中、英、法、日文亲共书籍，这些是我的朋友王日华 (          ) 留下的。他是广东人，去年春天已返回原籍。

我能略懂英语听说，但不会书写。我不懂日语的读、写、说。

(签名)   南连达。

pages.en:
Hou Ah Kung (          ).
Kiangwan, Kiangsu                  P. . . 11ts
Lousa           1.5.1933.                  Clerk Van Ti-foo.

    My name is Hou Ah Kung, aged 20, single, native of Kao King
Miao (          ), North of Kiangwan, Kiangsu, temporarily
employed as a coolie by the Chapei Electric Company.
    I went to school for one year when I was nine years of age,
in my native place, and I can read and write a little. Up till
November 1932 I worked on my farm - a small piece of ground which
had been left to me by my parents who are now both dead. In
November of last year a friend of mine named Ah Mao (          )
was instrumental in obtaining a position for me as a temporary
coolie in the battery room of the Chapei Electrical Works, where
he is working himself.    My diary is at present 55 cents per day
    At 7 a.m. to day I left my home in Kiangwan with the intentio
of visiting my brother Hou King Sung (          ) who is an
apprentice at the For Tsang "es (          ) Shoe Shop opposite
the Wayside Police Station.    I entered the Settlement by the
Stone Bridge and intended taking a tram but as they were all too
crowded I decided to walk there instead, via Sinza Road.    At the
corner of Sinza and Wenchow Roads I met a young Chinese male
dressed in foreign clothing who at that time was in possession of
some small paper banners.    This male asked me to join the Vol-
unteer Army and invited me to participate in a meeting at the
Public Recreation Ground, West Gate.    I made no reply to these
remarks.    Another foreign dressed male Chinese then approached
me, handed me the banners which the Police seized, and told me
to follow him and the other Chinese.    I did so.    We arrived at
the corner of Peking and Thibet Roads at about 11 a.m. when I was
arrested by a plain-clothes policeman, the other two men, whom I
do not know, making good their escape.
pages.zh:
侯阿公 (          )。
江苏江湾                  P. . . 11ts
老闸           1933.5.1.                  书记员 Van Ti-foo.

    本人姓名侯阿公，20岁，未婚，籍贯江苏江湾以北的高泾庙 (          )，目前在闸北电力公司临时受雇为苦力。
    9岁时，我在家乡上过一年学，能略识文字。直到1932年11月，我一直在自家农场劳作——那是一小块由现已双亡的父母留给我的土地。去年11月，我的朋友阿毛 (          ) 帮忙在闸北电厂电池间为我谋得一份临时苦力的职位，他本人也在那里工作。    我目前的日薪为5角5分。
    今天早上7点，我离开江湾的家，打算去探望我的兄弟侯景松 (          )，他是路边捕房对面福昌鞋店 (          ) 的学徒。    我经由石桥进入租界，本想乘坐电车，但因车内过于拥挤，我决定改走新闸路前往。    在新闸路与温州路转角处，我遇到一名身穿西装的年轻中国男子，当时他手中持有一些小纸旗。    该男子邀请我加入义勇军，并邀我参加西门公共游乐场的集会。    我对这些话未作回应。    随后另一名身穿西装的中国男子上前，将那些被警察查获的旗帜塞给我，并让我跟随他和另一名中国人。    我照做了。    我们于上午11点左右到达北京路与西藏路转角处，此时我被一名便衣巡捕逮捕，另外两名我不认识的男子则趁机逃脱。

pages.en:
Zau Tehing Zau (          ).
upeh                                D.S. Pitts.
Louss           1/5/1933            Clerk Van Ti Foo.

My name is Zau Tehing Zau, aged 32, single, native of
Hupeh, Chinese Foodshop cook by profession.
    I was born at Yang Sing Hsien (          ), Hupeh, where
my father was a farmer.    I have never been to school and can
neither read nor write.
    I came to Shanghai for the first time in 1928 from my
native place where I was a farmer.    Arriving here I resided
at a Chinese Foodshop on Ward Road near Chaenfoong Road, where
I remained for nearly three years, working there all the time.
From then until the time of my arrest I have been living and
working at 670 Jansen Road - premises housing the Foo Young
Euh (          ) Foodshop.
    This morning at 10 a.m. I left Jansen Road intending to
proceed on foot to a friend of mine named Zau who lives at
Jessfield Village.    When near the corner of Peking and Swei-
chow Roads I saw a crowd of people and being curious went to see
what was happening.    However I was arrested by an Indian Pol-
iceman though for what reason I do not know.
    I am not a communist and am not attached to any party.
I have never been approached by anyone with regard to any
radical matter.

                        Signed : Zau Tehing Zau.
pages.zh:
赵廷赵 (          )。
湖北                                D.S. Pitts.
老闸           1933/5/1            书记员 Van Ti Foo.

本人姓名赵廷赵，32岁，未婚，籍贯湖北，职业为中餐馆厨师。
    我出生于湖北阳新县 (          )，父亲是农民。    我从未上过学，既不识字也不会写字。
    1928年，我第一次从家乡（当时我是农民）来到上海。    抵达后，我居住在靠近新丰路的华德路一家中餐馆内，在那里住了将近三年，一直在此工作。    从那时起直到被捕，我一直居住并工作在詹森路670号——富荣欧 (          ) 餐馆所在地。
    今天上午10点，我离开詹森路，打算步行前往住在极司菲尔路村的一位姓赵的朋友家。    当走到北京路与苏州路转角附近时，我看到一群人，出于好奇便上前观看发生了什么事。    然而，我被一名印度巡捕逮捕，但我不知道原因。
    我不是共产党员，也不隶属于任何政党。    从未有人就任何激进事项接触过我。

                        签名 : 赵廷赵.

pages.en:
Zau Hou Foh (        )
Hupeh.                                D.S. Tilson.
Louza Stn.          1.5.33.           Clerk Fang Kuo Liang.

    My name is Zau Huo Foh, age 32, married, native of
Yan Shing Hsien (        ), Hupeh. I studied in a primary
school in the native village at the age of 7 for one and a
half years, after which I worked as a farmer. I came to
Shanghai for the first time in December 1927 when I was 25
years old. I was employed as a worker by the Zao Sheng Iron
Works, Haining Road, which I left 2 years later. Afterwards
I and my three brothers ran the Hong Shing Iron Works at
No.514 East Yuhang Road which is at present under the
management of my brothers. I am the proprietor of Tsung
Shing Kwan (        ) food shop at 559 Tien Pao Road, Hung
Tseng (        ), which I opened in August 1932.
    At 7 a.m. today I left my shop to proceed to Ponto
de Catherine, French Concession, to visit my friend. Whilst
I was walking along Thibet Road near Peking Road at about 10 a.m. I met
a crowd of people at the road corner. I saw the crowd throw
away pamphlets and run away. A few minutes later the Police
came and arrested me and took me to the Station. I did
not pick up any pamphlets from the street.

                                Signed: Zau Hou Foh.
pages.zh:
赵厚福 (        )
湖北.                                D.S. Tilson.
老闸捕房          1933.5.1.           书记员 方国良.

    本人姓名赵厚福，32岁，已婚，籍贯湖北盐兴县 (        )。7岁时，我在本村小学读书一年半，之后务农。1927年12月，我25岁时第一次来到上海。我被海宁路的肇生铁工厂雇佣为工人，两年后离职。后来，我和三个兄弟共同经营东余杭路514号的鸿兴铁工厂，目前该厂由我的兄弟们管理。我是洪升馆 (        ) 餐馆的老板，该馆位于虹口天宝路559号，于1932年8月开业。
    今天早上7点，我离开店铺，前往法租界凯瑟琳桥拜访朋友。    上午10点左右，当我走在靠近北京路的西藏路上时，在路口遇到一群人。我看到人群丢弃传单并四散逃跑。几分钟后，警察赶到并逮捕了我，将我带往捕房。我并未从街上捡拾任何传单。

                                签名: 赵厚福.

pages.en:
Wong Sz Yien (                ).
Haiming, Kiangsu.                 D?S. Pitts.
Lousa        1.5.1933.            Clerk Van Ti Foo.

    My name is Wong Sz Yien, aged 21, native of Haiming, Kiangsu,
single, residing at 60 Heong Feh Li (          ), Sinsa Road.
    I was born at Haiming, Kiangsu, where my parents, who own a
small food shop, are at present living.
    When I was eight years of age, I commenced studying at a
primary school in my native place and continued to do so for a
period of six years, and consequently I can read and write fairly
well.        At the age of 16 I came to Shanghai in order to be
apprenticed to the Tsoong Hwa (          ) Printing Works,
Thibet Road - I do not know the number, but the Police have visited
the address and verified my statement as being correct.        I
completed my apprenticeship in this concern when I was 19 years
of age, and am still employed with the same company, my salary at
present being $15 per month.
    A little after noon to-day after I had had my tiffin at the
Nam Yoong Ching (          ) Food Shop, I left the premises in-
tending to return to my place of employment.        Near the corner
of Peking and Thibet Roads I was arrested by an Indian Policeman,
but I do not know the reason for his action.        At the time of
leaving the foodshop I saw a crowd of people and a number of
handbills lying in the road.        I didn't distribute these
pamphlets, and I knew nothing about the four other accused, whom
I have never seen before.
    I am not a communist and not affiliated to any party.    I
have never been approached by anyone regarding anything apper-
taining to Communist movements.

            Signed :        Wong Sz Yien.
pages.zh:
黄思贤 (                )。
江苏海门.                 D?S. Pitts.
老闸        1933.5.1.            书记员 Van Ti Foo.

    本人姓名黄思贤，21岁，籍贯江苏海门，未婚，居住在新闸路香飞里60号 (          )。
    我出生于江苏海门，父母目前仍住在那里，经营一家小餐馆。
    8岁时，我在家乡开始上小学，持续了六年，因此我能较好地读写。        16岁时，我来到上海，在西藏路的中华印刷厂 (          ) 当学徒——我不知道门牌号，但警察已去过该地址并证实我的陈述属实。        19岁时，我在这家公司完成了学徒期，目前仍受雇于同一家公司，月薪现为15元。
    今天午后不久，我在南永庆 (          ) 餐馆吃完午饭后，离开那里打算返回工作地点。        在北京路与西藏路转角附近，我被一名印度巡捕逮捕，但我不知道他这样做的原因。        离开餐馆时，我看到一群人以及散落在路上的一些传单。        我没有分发这些传单，也不认识其他四名被告，我以前从未见过他们。
    我不是共产党员，也不隶属于任何政党。    从未有人就任何与共产主义运动有关的事项接触过我。

            签名 :        黄思贤.

CONFIDENTIAL
DRAWER

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
C. & S. B. REGISTRY
No. D 4801
Date 1 / 8 / 33

July 31, 3.

The Officer Commanding,
Special Branch.

I wish to put on record my appreciation
of the most excellent work done by Superintendent
T. Robertson in police action to prevent and
suppress agitation which aimed at causing distur-
bances on May 1 and other anniversaries. The work
performed by the Special Branch on the eve of such
anniversaries has done more than anything else
towards ensuring peace on the actual anniversary
days. I appreciate very much the work done by
Superintendent T. Robertson in this connection.

(Sd) F. W. Gerrard
Commissioner of Police.

File
MB
JULY 31 1933

刑事侦缉处登记室
编号 D 4801
日期 1933年8月1日

1933年7月31日。

特别处处长，

我希望记录在案，我对T. Robertson警司在防止和镇压旨在引起5月1日及其他纪念日骚乱的煽动活动中的警务行动中所做的极其出色的工作表示赞赏。特别处在这些纪念日前夕所做的工作，对于确保实际纪念日当天的和平起到了比其他任何事情都更大的作用。我非常赞赏T. Robertson警司在此方面所做的工作。

（签名）F. W. Gerrard
警务处长。

归档
MB
1933年7月31日

Extract from Monthly Report for
May 1933

On May I, encounters between the Municipal Police
and people bent on creating disturbances occurred in
the vicinity of the junctions of Thorburn and Wayside
Roads, North Kiangse and Haining Roads, Wenchow and Avenue
Roads, and Chefoo and Peking Roads. There were about 100
people in the crowd at the first mentioned place, about 80
at the second, about 20 at the third and about 80 at the last.
During these collisions the Police seized considerable
quantities of Communist handbills and took 26 persons into
custody. Of the prisoners, 10 were sentenced to various terms
of imprisonment ranging from 6 months to 5 years and 2 months,
1 was released on security, 12 were acquitted and released, and one,
a Formosan, was handed over to the Japanese Authorities. The
remaining two were transferred to Chinese controlled territory
for trial, and a similar decision was reached in the case of
three persons who were taken into custody in the course of
visits made to various addresses as a sequel to the arrests in
the streets. Thirty one others apprehended under similar
circumstances were released.

1933年5月月报摘录

5月1日，工部局警察与蓄意制造骚乱的人群在陶尔斐司路与韦斯特路交界处、江西北路与海宁路交界处、温州路与阿维农路交界处、以及芝罘路与北京路交界处附近发生冲突。第一个地点的人群约有100人，第二个地点约80人，第三个地点约20人，最后一个地点约80人。在这些冲突中，警方查获了大量共产主义传单，并拘留了26人。在被捕者中，10人被判处6个月至5年2个月不等的有期徒刑，1人获保释，12人被判无罪释放，还有一名台湾人被移交给日本当局。其余两人被移送至中国管辖区域受审，对在街头逮捕后随后对各地址进行走访过程中拘留的三人也作出了类似决定。另外三十一名在类似情况下被捕的人被释放。

D48M

MEMORANDUM

Labour Day Demonstrations and raiding of branches of
People's Self Salvation Association to Resist Insult
by the Municipal Police

This anniversary was taken advantage of by
members of the "People's Self Salvation Association to
Resist Insult" to stage demonstrations which, however,
was effectively dispersed by the Municipal Police and
Chinese Authorities.

The fact that several members of the Association
arrested during a demonstration on Thorburn Road were in
possession of communistic literature while other participants
discarded in their flight bundles of leaflets of a like
nature is an indication that the Communist Party is behind
the Association or is utilizing its (the Association's)
so-called patriotic activity to further "red" propaganda.

The following is a resume of the demonstrations
referred to above together with particulars of raids
carried out on the various bases of the Association
subsequent to the seizure of communistic literature
on Thorburn Road :-

Between 6 and 7.30 a.m. May 1 about 50 members
of the Eastern District Branch of the People's Self
Salvation Association to Resist Insult assembled
in the office at No.28 Soong Mur Li, Sungpan Road,
and at 7.40 a.m. proceeded to a vacant piece of
ground at the corner of Thornurn and Wayside Roads.
On their arrival they were joined by another party
of 50 persons and a meeting was held, in the course
of which speeches were made, slogans shouted and
handbills bearing on the Anniversary in question

D48M

备忘录

劳动节示威及工部局警察搜查“抗日救国会”分会

该纪念日被“抗日救国会”成员利用来进行示威活动，但这些活动被工部局警察和中国当局有效驱散。

在陶尔斐司路的示威活动中被捕的几名协会成员持有共产主义文献，而其他参与者在逃跑时丢弃了成捆的类似性质的传单，这一事实表明共产党在协会背后支持，或者正在利用其（协会的）所谓爱国活动来推进“红色”宣传。

以下是上述示威活动的摘要，以及在陶尔斐司路查获共产主义文献后对协会各个据点进行的搜查详情：

5月1日上午6时至7时30分之间，约50名“抗日救国会”东区分会成员聚集在宋潘路宋慕里28号的办公室，并于上午7时40分前往陶尔斐司路与韦斯特路拐角处的一块空地。到达后，另一批50人加入了他们，并举行了会议，期间有人发表演讲，高呼口号，并分发与该纪念日有关的传单

Application will be made to Court to-day for

Of the remaining nine prisoners, eight are charged

During the early afternoon the Chinese
Authorities arrested in the vicinity of the Public

Of the 60 persons arrested on this anniversary,

of detention for two days to permit of further
investigation being made, while 13 who were charged

assaulting the police were remanded sine die. On
May 3, as a result of an identification parade, ten
of the prisoners were recognized as having conducted
communistic activity in Chinese controlled territory.

今日将向法庭申请对59名被捕者中的50人签发为期一周的拘留令，以便警方调查上述协会成员如何持有声称源自共产党的传单。在其余九名囚犯中，八人被控袭击警察，第九人被控阻碍警察执行公务。针对他们的案件，也将出于同样目的申请还押候审。

午后早些时候，中国当局在西门公共游乐场附近逮捕了36名持有横幅和传单的人员。

在此次纪念日逮捕的60人中，一名台湾人被移交给日本领事当局，其余人员于5月2日被提堂，其中46人被签发为期两天的拘留令，以便进行进一步调查，而13名被控分发共产主义文献和/或袭击警察的人则被无限期还押候审。5月3日，经过列队辨认，十名囚犯被指认曾在中国管辖区域内从事共产主义活动。

Of the prisoners on writ of detention, 40 were on May 4
released by Court owing to lack of evidence to support
charges of communistic activity , and another was
likewise liberated on May 9. Of the remaining 18
prisoners, 14 appeared before Court on remand on May 17
when five were extradited to the Chinese Authorities and
9 were further remanded until May 23 when two were each
sentenced to 5 years and 2 months, one to 5 years, two
to 2 years and 6 months, one to 6 months and one released
on furnishing security while the remaining two were found
not guilty.

The remaining four of the persons arrested appeared
before Court on remand on May 30 on a charge of
disseminating communistic literature. One was sentenced
to 5 years' imprisonment and three each to two and a
half years.

在被拘留令羁押的囚犯中，40人因缺乏支持共产主义活动指控的证据，于5月4日由法庭释放，另一人亦于5月9日获释。在剩余的18名囚犯中，14人于5月17日出庭受审，其中五人被引渡给中国当局，9人还押至5月23日，届时两人各被判刑5年零2个月，一人被判刑5年，两人被判刑2年零6个月，一人被判刑6个月，一人在提供担保后获释，其余两人被判无罪。

其余四名被捕者于5月30日以散布共产主义文献的罪名出庭受审。其中一人被判监禁5年，三人各被判监禁两年半。

Political

International Labour Day - May 1 - possible activities
of communist and radical

Fifteen different kinds of communistic leaflets which
have come into the hands of the Municipal Police in the
past few days contain the usual stereotyped exhortations to
the toiling masses to stage demonstrations, meetings and
processions to demand better working conditions and the
overthrow of the Kuomintang and the Japanese capitalists.
This propaganda coupled with information obtained by agents
indicates that local reds will carry out the usual series of
small flying demonstrations and surreptitious dissemination
of pamphlets.

The People's Self Salvation Association to Resist
Insult, a body promoted by firebrands who are suspected of
being backed by the Communist Party, is feverishly engaged
in preparing large quantities of literature and other
paraphernalia for a mass meeting which it hopes to convene
on the Public Recreation Ground on the above day and as it
has been definitely laid down by the Chinese Authorities that
any such gathering will be prohibited, the would-be
demonstrators will in all probability turn their attention
to the Settlement, especially the Japanese mill areas.
The Headquarters of this association are located at 15 I
Yuen Li (怡芳里), Carter Road (Sinsa District) with branches

政治类

国际劳动节——5月1日——共产党及激进分子的可能活动

过去几天落入工部局警务处手中的十五种不同种类的共产主义传单，包含通常陈词滥调式的鼓动，号召劳苦大众举行示威、集会和游行，要求改善工作条件，推翻国民党和日本资本家。这种宣传加上特工获得的情报表明，当地的“赤色分子”将进行一系列惯常的小规模飞行示威，并秘密散发小册子。

“民众救国会”（People's Self Salvation Association to Resist Insult）是一个由疑似得到共产党支持的煽动者推动的组织，正狂热地准备大量文献和其他物品，希望于上述日期在公共游乐场召开群众大会。由于中国当局已明确规定禁止此类集会，潜在的示威者很可能会将注意力转向租界，特别是日本纱厂区域。该协会总部设在辛斯区（Sinsa District）卡特路（Carter Road）怡芳里15号，分部地址如下：

6) 要求为失业者提供救济和工作。
7) 反对虐待童工。
8) 调查日货储存情况；救济失业工人。
9) 推翻黄色工会领袖。
10) 支持苏维埃政府的劳动法。

April 30, 1933. Morning Translation.

MISCELLANEOUS

China Times and other local newspapers:-

LABOURERS TO OBSERVE LABOUR DAY

The Shanghai General Labour Union has published
the following notice :-

"May 1 being the International Labour Anniversary
Day all labourers should hold meetings to celebrate the day.
This Union will hold a meeting of labour representatives at
9 a.m. May 1 at the office of the Youths Propaganda Group,
Small West Gate."

Authorities to Adopt Precautionary Measures
Throughout Month of May.

The authorities of Chinese territory, the
International Settlement and the French Concession will
adopt precautionary measures from May 1 to 31.
The Public Safety Bureau will detail double
post duty men every day while the motor-cycle corps will
patrol streets. The various Police Stations of the
International Settlement and the French Concession will
also adopt precautionary measures.
On May 1 all the local authorities will
adopt precautionary measures from 1 a.m.

当局将在整个五月采取预防措施。

5月1日，所有地方当局将从凌晨1点起采取预防措施。

Communist Propaganda

The following communist pamphlets were obtained
by the Municipal Police in Western Chapei on April 24,
1933 :-

(1) Pamphlet entitled "Manifesto relating to May 1
Anniversary", purporting to have emanated from the
Central Committee of the Chinese Communist Party.
This document, apart from denouncing the Kuomintang
and other foreign Imperialists as being obstacles
to the emancipation of the labouring masses,
exhorts all labourers, peasants, students,
soldiers, refugees and the toiling masses to
commemorate the May 1 Anniversary by declaring
strikes and holding demonstrations, to struggle
for their emancipation, to start a national
revolutionary war, to support Soviet Russia, and
the Red Armies, to demand improved working
conditions and to join the Chinese Communist
Party.

(2) Pamphlet entitled "Outline of Propaganda for the
May 1 Anniversary", purporting to have emanated
from the Propaganda Department of the Kiangsu
Provincial Committee of the Chinese Communist
Party. This document, apart from outlining
the significance of the occasion, exhorts the
people to oppose the capitalists, the foreign
Imperialists, the Kuomintang, the Yellow labour
unions and other reactionary cliques, and to
carry out their struggles in accordance with
the Bolshevik doctrine.
pages.zh:
共产党宣传

以下共产党小册子由警务处于1933年4月24日在闸北西部查获：-

(1) 小册子题为《五一纪念宣言》，声称出自中国共产党中央委员会。该文件除了谴责国民党和其他外国帝国主义者是劳动群众解放的障碍外，还号召所有工人、农民、学生、士兵、难民和劳苦大众通过宣布罢工和举行示威来纪念五一，为他们的解放而斗争，发动民族革命战争，支持苏俄和红军，要求改善工作条件，并加入中国共产党。

(2) 小册子题为《五一纪念宣传大纲》，声称出自中国共产党江苏省委宣传部。该文件除了概述该节日的意义外，还号召人民反对资本家、外国帝国主义者、国民党、黄色工会和其他反动派系，并按照布尔什维克主义进行斗争。

pages.en:
Summarized translation of a communist pamphlet entitled "Manifesto
relating to May 1 Anniversary", purporting to have emanated from the
Central Committee of the Chinese Communist Party, which was found
by the Municipal Police in Western Chapei on April 24, 1933.

Labourers, peasants and toiling masses throughout the country,

The May 1st Anniversary is a day when the revolutionary
strength of the proletariat class will be examined. To commemorate
this day we should struggle for the emancipation of the labouring
masses of the world as well as for the final victory of the
Chinese revolution.
The labourers in Sovietized nations instead of being
harrassed by unemployment, starvation and warfare as labourers
in other places are, have secured their own emancipation. The
labouring masses of various nations at present comprehend that
only by revolution or by following the way adopted by the labourers
of Soviet Russia can be emancipated.
This year Imperialism is in a more critical state. The
Japanese with the aid of the French and British Imperialists
have invaded and occupied Manchuria and Jehol and have built
up a base for attacking the Soviet in future. Therefore on
the May 1st Anniversary of this year, we should oppose the
Imperialistic war and support the proletariat Soviet.
The Kuomintang in order to save itself from the present
crisis solicits assistance from the Imperialists in suppressing
the people's revolution. It has not only sold the Three
Eastern Provinces and Shanghai, but is negotiating with Japan
for the sale of the whole nation. With this aim in view,
the Kuomintang mobilizes troops throughout the country to attack
the sole armed force of the people, the labourers and peasants'
Red Army and the Soviet political administration. Should
Chinese people wish to remain in existence and to be emancipated,
they should process to start a revolutionary war to beat down
Imperialism and its running dog, the Kuomintang.
Soviet China is antagonistic against the Kuomintang.
In Soviet districts the influence of the Imperialists has
been eradicated and the reactionary rule of the Kuomintang
pulled down, whilst labourers and peasants are vested with
political power. Furthermore, land is divided amongst the
peasant masses, Labour Law promulgated, and an 8-hour working
day put in force. The Soviet and the Red Army have announced
their readiness to fight against Japanese Imperialism and would
have led the people throughout the nation to drive out the
Japanese and other Imperialists from the country had not the
Kuomintang surrounded them with 800,000 troops. Should the
Chinese people wish to struggle for their emancipation for
national independence and for national unification, they should
oppose the attack on the Soviet districts by the Kuomintang
and protect the Soviet administration and the Red Army.
Only the Soviet can save China from the present perilous
state.
Toiling masses throughout the nation, rise up to
commemorate the May 1st Anniversary. Unite and arm yourselves
to start the national revolutionary war, oppose the attacks
of the Japanese imperialists, oppose the partition of China
and the attack on Soviet Russia by the Imperialists, oppose
the attack on Soviet districts and the Red Army, and demand
that the troops throughout the country be mobilized and despatched
to fight against the Japanese imperialists, and to fight for the
victory of the Chinese revolution. The present situation
is tense. Hundreds and thousands of the toiling masses
have been rendered homeless and now face starvation and death
as a result of the pillaging and massacre carried out by the
Japanese Imperialists and the internecine warfare of the
Kuomintang militarists. Under the administration of the
Kuomintang, none of the factories are well constructed and none
of the workers hold 'Social Insurance policies'. The tragedy
of the Tseng Tai Rubber Factory is to be noted.
Labourers, declare strikes and enforce your demands
for an 8-hour working day, increase in wages, relief

1933年4月24日，公共租界警务处在闸北西部查获一份题为《五一纪念宣言》的共产主义小册子，该小册子声称出自中国共产党中央委员会。以下是其摘要译文。

全国劳工、农民及劳苦大众们：

五一纪念日是检验无产阶级革命力量的日子。为纪念这一节日，我们应为世界劳苦大众的解放以及中国革命的最终胜利而斗争。

苏维埃国家的劳工不像其他地方的劳工那样遭受失业、饥饿和战乱的困扰，而是已经获得了自身的解放。目前，各国劳苦大众认识到，只有通过革命或遵循苏俄劳工所采取的道路，才能获得解放。

今年，帝国主义处于更加危急的状态。日本在法英帝国主义的帮助下，入侵并占领了满洲和热河，并为将来进攻苏联建立了基地。因此，在今年的五一纪念日，我们应反对帝国主义战争，支持无产阶级苏维埃。

国民党为了从当前的危机中自救，乞求帝国主义协助镇压人民革命。它不仅出卖了东三省和上海，而且正在与日本谈判出卖整个国家。出于这一目的，国民党在全国动员军队，攻击人民唯一的武装力量——工农红军和苏维埃政权。如果中国人民希望生存并获得解放，他们就应该发动革命战争，打倒帝国主义及其走狗国民党。

苏维埃中国与国民党相对立。在苏维埃地区，帝国主义的影响已被根除，国民党的反动统治被推翻，劳工和农民掌握了政治权力。此外，土地在农民群众中进行了分配，颁布了劳动法，并实行了八小时工作制。苏维埃和红军已宣布准备抗击日本帝国主义，若非国民党以80万军队包围他们，他们本已领导全国人民将日本及其他帝国主义驱逐出中国。如果中国人民希望为自身解放、民族独立和国家统一而斗争，他们就应反对国民党对苏维埃地区的进攻，保卫苏维埃政权和红军。

只有苏维埃才能将中国从目前的危险状态中拯救出来。

全国劳苦大众们，起来纪念五一节。团结起来，武装起来，发动民族革命战争，反对日本帝国主义的进攻，反对帝国主义瓜分中国和进攻苏俄，反对进攻苏维埃地区和红军，要求动员全国军队开赴前线抗击日本帝国主义，为中国革命的胜利而战。当前局势紧张。由于日本帝国主义的掠夺和屠杀以及国民党军阀的内战，成千上万的劳苦大众流离失所，面临饥饿和死亡。在国民党的统治下，没有一家工厂建设良好，也没有工人拥有“社会保险单”。曾泰橡胶厂的悲剧值得注意。

劳工们，举行罢工，坚持你们关于八小时工作制、增加工资、失业救济

Peasants, oppose exhorbitant taxes and high interest

Down with the "Yellow" labour unions!

和“社会保险”的要求，并通过举行示威游行和群众大会来纪念五一节。

农民们，反对苛捐杂税和高利贷；为土地革命而斗争，组织农民自卫队，开展游击战和武装起义，反对地主和国民党政府，建立苏维埃政权。

士兵们，拒绝攻打中国同胞，反对进攻苏维埃地区，要求开赴前线抗击日本，反对卖国的国民党政府。

难民们，团结起来，要求救济、食物和住所，反对造成你们苦难的国民党及帝国主义。举行罢工和示威游行以纪念五一节。

打倒“黄色”工会！

拒绝支付租金和债务，要求获得耕种的土地！

打倒将东三省和热河出卖给帝国主义的国民党！

支持苏维埃和红军，反对国民党对他们的进攻！

勇敢加入中国共产党，为中国革命的胜利而斗争！

中国共产党万岁，中国革命的唯一领导者！

Summarized Translation of a Communist Pamphlet entitled
"Outline of Propaganda for the May 1 Anniversary", purporting
to have emanated from the Propaganda Department of the
Kiangsu Provincial Committee of the Chinese Communist Party,
which was obtained by the Municipal Police in Western Chapel
on April 24, 1933.

1) May 1st is the Anniversary of the International Labour Day.
Labourers throughout the world should demand on this day
the enforcement of the 8-hour working day system and
struggle for their interests.

2) The economic conditions of the Imperialist countries this
year are becoming worse and as a consequence capitalists
intensify their oppression of the labourers. The latter,
however, in their counter-attack against oppression,
have organized strikes in various places. In Shanghai
over 400,000 workers have been dismissed and become unemployed
as a result of the enforcement by the foreign as well as
the Chinese capitalists of the 'rational production scheme'.
Those who are still employed are given more work but receive
less pay and are from time to time assaulted, insulted or
treacherously treated by the capitalists. The Kuomintang
and 'yellow' labour unions have surrendered to the Japanese
and other imperialists assisting them in suppressing strikes
or other struggles organized by the labourers. Japan
with the aid of the Kuomintang has occupied Jehol, while
Peiping and Tientsin are under the bombardment of Japanese
aeroplanes.

3) In Soviet Russia the first 'Five Year Plan' has been accomplished,
the 7-hour working day enforced, and the livelihood
of labourers improved. In the Chinese Soviet districts,
labourers enjoy equal treatment.
The Imperialists are ever planning an attack on Soviet
Russia; the Chinese-Eastern Railway problem and the arrest
of British engineers by Soviet Russia are instances thereof.
The Kuomintang and other reactionary parties have been
endeavouring to eliminate the red armies with a view to
saving their perilous rule. But, contrary to their
expectation, the red armies which are being enthusiastically
supported by the labouring and peasant masses, have
succeeded in dissolving several divisions of the Kuomintang
army. Commanders of the 52nd, 59th and 27th Divisions
were either killed or captured alive.

4) May 1st is approaching. We should therefore organize
strikes to oppose the capitalists, the Kuomintang, the
'yellow' labour unions and other reactionary parties.
a) Workers of cotton mills and tobacco factories,
seamen and railway employees should join their respective
unions and the Communist Party, and carry out counter-
attacks against the Kuomintang and capitalists under
the guide of the Communist Party and the Federation of
Labour Unions (old Labour Federation). Demand an increase
in wages, the enforcement of the 8-hour working day.
b) Extend the anti-Imperialist and anti-
Japanese movements, intensify the boycott movement,
stage theatrical performances for raising funds for the
relief of the North-Eastern refugees, organize "Donation
Groups" and "Medical Corps" to proceed to the North,
organize National Salvation Associations and organize
self-defence armed forces of the branches of the Association
and extend the movement to welcome the "Ba-pi-sair",
Anti-Imperialistic Delegation.

1933年4月24日，公共租界警务处在闸北西部（原文误作Chapel，应为Chapei）查获一份题为《五一纪念宣传大纲》的共产主义小册子，该小册子声称出自中国共产党江苏省委员会宣传部。以下是其摘要译文。

1) 五月一日是国际劳动节纪念日。全世界的劳工应在这一天要求实行八小时工作制，并为争取自身利益而斗争。

2) 今年帝国主义国家的经济状况日益恶化，资本家因此加剧了对劳工的压迫。然而，劳工在反击压迫的过程中，已在各地组织了罢工。在上海，由于外国和中国资本家实施“生产合理化方案”，超过40万工人被解雇而失业。那些仍有工作的人工作量增加但工资减少，并时常受到资本家的殴打、侮辱或欺诈性对待。国民党和“黄色”工会已向日本及其他帝国主义投降，协助他们镇压劳工组织的罢工或其他斗争。日本在国民党的帮助下占领了热河，而北平和天津正遭受日本飞机的轰炸。

3) 在苏俄，第一个“五年计划”已完成，七小时工作制得以实行，劳工的生活水平得到改善。在中国苏维埃地区，劳工享有平等待遇。
帝国主义一直在策划进攻苏俄；中东路问题和苏俄逮捕英国工程师便是例证。国民党及其他反动党派一直试图消灭红军，以挽救其危殆的统治。但是，与他们的预期相反，得到劳苦大众和农民群众热情支持的红军，已成功瓦解了国民党的几个师。第52师、第59师和第27师的指挥官或被击毙或被生俘。

4) 五一节即将来临。因此，我们应组织罢工，反对资本家、国民党、“黄色”工会及其他反动党派。
a) 棉纺厂和烟草厂的工人、海员及铁路员工应加入各自的工会和共产党，并在共产党和工会联合会（旧工会联合会）的指导下，对国民党和资本家进行反击。要求增加工资，实行八小时工作制。
b) 扩大反帝国主义和反日本运动，加强抵制运动，上演戏剧为东北难民筹款救济，组织“捐款团”和“医疗队”北上，组织救国会并组织该会分支机构的自卫武装力量，扩大欢迎“巴比塞”（Barbusse，音译）反帝国主义代表团的活动。

Summarized Translation of a Communist Pamphlet entitled
"Outline of Propaganda for the May 1 Anniversary", purporting
to have emanated from the Propaganda Department of the
Kiangsu Provincial Committee of the Chinese Communist Party,
which was obtained by the Municipal Police in Western Chapel
on April 24,1933.

1) May 1st if the Anniversary of the International Labour Day.
Labourers throughout the world should demand on this day
the enforcement of the 8-hour working day system and
struggle for their interests.

2) The economic conditions of the Imperialist countries this
year are becoming worse and as a consequence capitalists
intensify their oppression of the labourers. The latter,
however, in their counter-attack against oppression,
have organized strikes in various places. In Shanghai
over 400,000 workers have been dismissed and become unemployed
as a result of the enforcement by the foreign as well as
the Chinese capitalists of the 'rational production scheme'.
Those who are still employed are given more work but receive
less pay and are from time to time assaulted, insulted or
treacherously treated by the capitalists. The Kuomintang
and 'yellow' labour unions have surrendered to the Japanese
and other imperialists assisting them in suppressing strikes
or other struggles organized by the labourers. Japan
with the aid of the Kuomintang has occupied Jehol, while
Peiping and Tientsin are under the bombardment of Japanese
aeroplanes.

3) In Soviet Russia the first 'Five Year Plan' has been accompli-
-shed, the 7-hour working day enforced, and the livelihood
of labourers improved. In the Chinese Soviet districts,
labourers enjoy equal treatment.
The Imperialists are ever planning an attack on Soviet
Russia; the Chinese-Eastern Railway problem and the arrest
of British engineers by Soviet Russia are instances thereof.
The Kuomintang and other reactionary parties have been
endeavouring to eliminate the red armies with a view to
saving their perilous rule. But, contrary to their
expectation, the red armies which are being enthusiastically
supported by the labouring and peasant masses, have
succeeded in dissolving several divisions of the Kuomintang
army. Commanders of the 52nd, 59th and 27th Divisions
were either killed or captured alive.

4) May 1st is approaching. We should therefore organize
strikes to oppose the capitalists, the Kuomintang, the
'yellow' labour unions and other reactionary parties.
a) Workers of cotton mills and tobacco factories,
seamen and railway employees should join their respective
unions and the Communist Party, and carry out counter-
attacks against the Kuomintang and capitalists under
the guide of the Communist Party and the Federation of
Labour Unions (old Labour Federation). Demand an increase
in wages, the enforcement of the 8-hour working day, etc.
b) Extend the anti-Imperialist and anti-
Japanese movements, intensify the boycott movement,
stage theatrical performances for raising funds for the
relief of the North-Eastern refugees, organize "Consolation
Groups" and "Medical Corps" to proceed to the North,
organize National Salvation Associations and organize
self-defence armed forces of the branches of the Association
and extend the movement to welcome the "Ba-pi-sair"
Anti-Imperialistic Delegation.

Date April 30, 1933.

Subject (in full) Proposed communistic activities on May 1 - International Labour Day.

Made by D.I. Kuh Pao-hwa. Forwarded by [Signature]

Agents A-4257, 1263 and 1582 report that workers
of various industrial concerns in Western Chapei have planned
to meet at Tsu Ka Jao (周家桥) at about 7 a.m. May 1 and
then march to Zau Ka Doo (Jessfield). They will then proceed
to the Kawamura Memorial Tower. Here they will be joined
by a number of other workers under the leadership of one
Li Siau Oo Tsz (李小五子), reported to be Secretary of the
Shanghai Western Special District Committee of the Chinese
Communist Party. The participants will then separate and
proceed to the following places :-
(1) N.W.K.Nos.3 and 4 Cotton Mills,19 Soochow Road.
(2) Sung Sing No.2 Cotton Mill, 2/3 Ichang Road.
(3) N.W.K.Nos 5 and 7 Cotton Mills,14 W.Soochow Road.
(4) N.W.K.No.8 Cotton Mill, 146 Gordon Road.
(5) N.W.K.No.9 Cotton Mill, 640 Markham Road.
(6) Wing On No.3 Cotton Mill, 491 Markham Road,
for the purpose of holding demonstrations after which they
will again congregate in the vicinity of the Markham Road
Bridge at about 10.45 a.m. The demonstrators will then
move to the direction of Thibet Road near Peking Road, via
Avenue and Sinza Roads. Here, they will await the arrival
of a representative from the Kiangsu Provincial Committee
who will lead them to participate in the proposed general
meeting of citizens' representatives to be convened by the
"People's Self-Salvation Association to Resist Insults" on
the Public Recreation Ground, West Gate, at about 1 p.m.
Information indicates that the workers in the
Eastern District will assemble in the vicinity of Dalny and
Pingliang Roads and then proceed in isolated groups to

10 p.m. 30.4.33 From Supt. Robertson,

With reference to May 1st report information indicates
that labour adherents of the Communist Party will attempt to
hold demonstrations in the vicinity of Japanese mills in
West District during the early forenoon intending participation
of the mass meeting will, prepare to proceed to West Gate in
small parties, meet at the following points about 11 a.m:
Range Road near N.Szechuen Road.
Thibet and Peking Road corner.
Sungpan Road.
Dalny and Pingliang Road corner.
Thorburn and Baikal Roads.
Markham Road Bridge.

A further unconfirmed report is to the effect that Reds
plan to gather on The Bund between 8 and 9 a.m. and thereafter
proceed to the Soviet Consulate where they will hold a
demonstration.

Reg. Please archive to file.

May 5 Anniversary - Kuomintang observance
In observance of the Anniversary of the Assumption
of Office by the late Dr. Sun Yat-sen in the Canton

a meeting of representatives of local public bodies
in its Headquarters, West Gate, at 9 a.m. May 5. The
Tangpu also notified the local community on May 2 to
observe the May 5 Anniversary by taking a holiday for
one day and hoisting flags.

五月五纪念日 - 国民党纪念活动
为纪念已故孙中山博士于1921年在广州政府就职周年纪念日，本地国民党将于5月5日上午9点在其西门总部召开本地公共团体代表会议。党部亦于5月2日通知本地社区，通过放假一天和悬挂旗帜来庆祝五月五纪念日。

All those arrested with the exception of one named

suffering from a scalp wound admitted that they were members
of the Eastern District Branch of the People's Self

Kwan Tseng Yoong, 1st on the list of the accused
claimed to be the unpaid chairman of the Eastern District
Branch of the People's Self Salvation Association to Resist
Insult, situated at 28 Sung Mou Li, Sungpang Road, and
stated that all the literature seized by the Yulin Road
officers had been brought to the above address, his residence,
and concurrently office of the Eastern Branch of the People's
Self Salvation Association to Resist Insult, by eight persons
who were arrested together with him and who stated they had
received same from the Headquarter Section of the Association
at No.15 I Yoen Li, Carter Road, at 6 a.m. on May 1.
In answer to questions "Kwan" stated that he did
not trouble to look at the pamphlets upon their arrival nor
did he ascertain if any of the members attending the "Branch
Office" had brought any literature other than that issued by
the Association with them.
The remaining seven persons in custody at Yulin
Road Station were interrogated and all claimed to have no
knowledge of the nature of the pamphlets found in their
possession.

At 5.30 p.m. all those arrested at No.15
I Yoen Li, Carter Road, were handed over the Yulin Road
and removed there under escort.
The Northern Branch of the People's Self
Salvation Association to Resist Insult, No.188 Tien Foh
Li, Range Road, was visited at about 6.40 p.m. and was
found unoccupied but a small quantity of literature bearing
on the activities of the Association was seized.
Thus the number of persons arrested as the
result of operations from Yulin Road Station at the
conclusion of the day was 43.
The nine persons arrested by Yulin Road at
8.50 a.m. May 1 were charged collectively with activities
subversive to the internal security of the State and severally
with assault on and obstructing the Police.
It was arranged by the People's Self Salvation
Association to Resist Insult, to hold a mass meeting on
the Public Recreation Ground, Nantao, at 12 noon and it
was left to the various branches to collect their members
and proceed to the venue.
Whilst en route to the scene of the projected
meeting various of the branch representatives clashed with
the police resulting in some of their number being arrested

Evan Tseng Yoong (管正荣)
Yangchow, Kiangpeh D. S. Sansom
Mulin Rd Stn May 1, 1933, Clerk Rao Yen-keng

My name is Evan Tseng Yoong, a coolie, age 44, native of Yangchow. At present I am unemployed, but act as the unpaid Chairman of the Eastern District Branch of the People's Self Salvation Association to Resist Insult.

On March 24, 1933, one of my friends named Tsai Ching-shi (蔡錦山), a food caterer employed at the Shanghai Cotton Mill No.3, and at present living in an upstairs room of a hot water shop on Sungpan Road, north of the Sacred Heart Hospital, together with two others named Zung Ah-nyi (鄭亞尼) and Waung (汪) respectively, came to my home at 28 Soong Bur Li, Sungpan Road, and asked to rent the downstairs front room at a rental of $10 per month. Tsai and Waung gave me three pamphlets bearing the stamp of the above association. We took these pamphlets to Yangtzepoo Station to enquire whether they were permitted to establish a branch of the Association at my home. The interpreter informed us that "the movement is patriotic and you had better go away; don't let the foreigners laugh at the Chinese". I therefore, considered that the movement was legal and the room was then rented to my friends. On March 26, I accepted an invitation to join the Association. Later, on this day, I went to the Kiangsu Fellow Countrymen's Association, Lane 100, 25 Sungpan Road, at the request of and accompanied by Zung Ah-nyi, who I learned was sent by the General Office of the People's Self Salvation Association to direct the activities of the Eastern District Branch, and made the
pages.zh:
管正荣（Evan Tseng Yoong）
扬州，江北 特别侦探桑森（D. S. Sansom）
木林路捕房 1933年5月1日，书记员饶燕庚（Rao Yen-keng）

我叫管正荣，苦力，44岁，扬州人。目前失业，但担任“民众自救会抵制侮辱”东区分会的义务主席。

1933年3月24日，我的一位朋友蔡锦山（Tsai Ching-shi），系上海第三棉纺厂雇用的伙食承办人，现居住在圣心医院以北宋潘路一家热水店楼上的房间里，他与另外两名分别名为郑亚尼（Zung Ah-nyi）和汪（Waung）的人来到我在宋潘路松茂里28号的家中，要求以每月10元的租金租用楼下前间。蔡和汪给了我三本盖有上述协会印章的小册子。我们带着这些小册子去杨树浦捕房询问是否允许在我家设立协会分会。翻译告诉我们：“这个运动是爱国的，你们最好离开；不要让外国人嘲笑中国人”。因此，我认为该运动是合法的，随后将房间租给了我的朋友。3月26日，我接受邀请加入了该协会。当天晚些时候，应郑亚尼的要求并由其陪同——我得知他是受民众自救会总会派遣来指导东区分会活动的——我前往宋潘路25号100弄江苏同乡会，并与

pages.en:
- 2 -
arrangements with the Fellow Countrymen's Association to hold
a meeting on its premises. A meeting was held by the
Branch in the Fellow Countrymen's Association premises on the
same day, some 30 or 40 people of the labouring class being
present. I did not attend the meeting. I attended the
second meeting of the Branch at the same address on April 2,
some 20 persons being present, and I was elected Chairman
of the Eastern District Branch. Although I was the
Chairman of the Branch, the affairs of the organisation
were left to the direction of Zung Ah-nyi and others.
<u>Yu Mai visited me on March 26, 1933, at my home</u>
on one occasion only and instructed me to accept all
literature bearing the chop of the Association. I knew
the head office address but never had occasion to visit it.
At 6 a.m. to-day (May 1), about 10 persons including
myself, met at the Branch Office, Sungpan Road, and were led
to a vacant site on Thorburn Road by Zung Ah-nyi, to meet other
members of the Eastern District for the purpose of proceeding
to the West Gate. At 8 a.m. we were en route to the
West Gate with some pamphlets in our possession.
The literature was seized by the police when I and
a number of the party were arrested. I have no knowledge of
the character of the pamphlets. The literature was
actually brought to the Branch Office by the persons who
assembled at the office at 6 a.m. and who stated that they had
received same at 18 I Yuen Li, Carter Road. All of the
pages.zh:
- 2 -
同乡会安排在其会所举行会议。当天，分会在同乡会会所举行了一次会议，约有30或40名劳工阶层人士出席。我没有参加这次会议。4月2日，我在同一地址参加了分会的第二次会议，约有20人出席，我被选为东区分会主席。虽然我是分会主席，但该组织的事务由郑亚尼等人负责指导。
<u>余迈（Yu Mai）仅在1933年3月26日来过我家一次</u>
并指示我接收所有盖有协会印章的文献。我知道总部的地址，但从未有机会去那里。
今天（5月1日）上午6时，包括我在内的约10人在宋潘路的分会办公室集合，并由郑亚尼带领至韬朋路的一处空地，与东区的其他成员会合，目的是前往西门。上午8时，我们携带一些宣传小册子前往西门途中。
当我和部分同行者被捕时，文献被警方没收。我对这些小册子的性质一无所知。这些文献实际上是由早上6点在办公室集合的人带到分会办公室的，他们声称是在卡特路（Carter Road）伊园里18号收到的。所有

pages.en:
- 3 -
persons arrested and brought to the Yulin Road Station
together with me, with the exception of the person taken
to the hospital, were in the party who brought the
literature to the Branch. I know these persons as
members of the Association. As a rule any fresh
literature brought to the Branch is shown to me, but
on this occasion, I had no opportunity to notice its
character.

Signed : Kwan Tseng Yoeng.
pages.zh:
- 3 -
与我一起被捕并带到榆林路捕房的人，除被送往医院的一人外，都是将文献带到分会的那群人。我认识这些人，他们是协会的成员。通常，任何带到分会的新文献都会给我看，但在这次情况下，我没有机会注意其性质。

签名：管振荣（Kwan Tseng Yoeng）。

pages.en:
Kwei Tsung Yi (鄭亞尼)
Kiading (嘉定), Szechuan
Yulin Rd. St. 1/5/36
U.S.I. varant
Clerk Sung Loong Co.

My name is Kwei Tsung Yi (鄭亞尼), I am age 23 and a native
of Kiading (嘉定), Szechuan. I studied at my native place for
four years and I can read and write Chinese. Leaving school at
the age of 17 I enlisted in the 28th Nationalist Army and served
as a private soldier for 4 years in Szechuan. About the end
of 1932 I received a letter from a friend in Shanghai telling
me of the new patriotic movement and urging me to join the
North Eastern Volunteer Army. In response to the letter I
proceeded to Shanghai where I arrived in January (1933) and
at once went to the Dah Jong (大王) Temple, Sinza Road, with
several other Szechuanese who wished to join the North Eastern
Volunteer Army. The temple is used as a billet for the new
volunteers. During the next few weeks I heard of the People's
Self Salvation Association to Resist Insult and decided to join
this society. I went to the headquarters of the association at
48 Route Valley and became a member. I was later instructed to
report to the Eastern District Branch at No.28 Soong Mau Li
(松茂里), Sungpan Road. I went to this address and met the
officer in charge, one Kwei Tsung Yoong (管正榮), who appointed
me to work in the General Affairs Department. I received no
pay but was given food and lodgings. Kwei Tsung Yoong resided
in the room over the kitchen and I in the office of the house
at 28 Soong Mau Li.

A meeting of the General Committee of the People's Self
Salvation Association was held on April 29 to discuss plans for
May 1. It was decided that all members should meet on Thortman
Road at 8 a.m. May 1 and then proceed to the East Gate. On
pages.zh:
郑亚尼（Kwei Tsung Yi / 鄭亞尼）
四川嘉定（Kiading）
榆林路捕房 1936年5月1日
美国副领事 warrant（原文如此，可能指传票或拘票）
宋龙公司（Sung Loong Co.）职员

我叫郑亚尼（Kwei Tsung Yi / 鄭亞尼），23岁，四川嘉定人。我在家乡读了四年书，能读写中文。17岁离校后，我入伍国民革命军第二十八军，在四川当了4年列兵。1932年底左右，我收到上海一位朋友的来信，告知新的爱国运动情况，并敦促我加入东北义勇军。响应这封信，我前往上海，于（1933年）1月抵达，并立即与其他几位希望加入东北义勇军的四川人一起前往新闸路的大王（Dah Jong）庙。该庙被用作新志愿者的宿营地。在接下来的几周里，我听说了“民众自救会抵制侮辱”，决定加入该社。我前往谷贝路（Route Valley）48号的协会总部并成为会员。后来我接到指令，到宋潘路松茂里28号的东区分会报到。我去了这个地址，见到了负责人管正荣（Kwei Tsung Yoong），他任命我在总务部工作。我没有薪水，但提供食宿。管正荣住在28号松茂里房屋厨房上面的房间里，我住在该房屋的办公室里。

4月29日举行了民众自救会总委员会会议，讨论五一节的计划。决定所有会员于5月1日上午8时在韬曼路（Thortman Road，即韬朋路）集合，然后前往东门。在

pages.en:
Zung Yoh Kyi (    ), page 2.

April 30 a notification was received from headquarters (now
removed to No.15 I Yoon Li (19 7/1), Carter Road.) instructing
all members of the eastern branch to participate in the mass
meeting to be held at the est date on May 1. During the
afternoon of April 30 a large number of pamphlets bearing the
stamp of the society were brought to the eastern branch
office at 28 Soong Meu Li by a special messenger from the
headquarters at 15 I Yoon Li, Carter Road. There were four
different kinds of handbills and one cartoon. At 7.30 a.m.
May 1 several members came to the office at Soong Meu Li
and took bundles of the handbills. We all then went to
Thorburn Road as arranged. Shortly after our arrival there
the police arrived and those persons in possession of the
handbills threw them on the ground and ran away. The
only handbills I saw were those bearing the stamp of the
People's Self Salvation Association to Resist Insult. I did
not see any communist handbills and if there were any I do
not know where they came from. I am not a communist and I
have never had any connection with the communist party.

(Signed) Zung Yoh Kyi.
pages.zh:
郑耀基（Zung Yoh Kyi），第2页。

4月30日，收到总部（现已迁至卡特路伊园里15号（19 7/1））的通知，指示东区分会所有成员参加定于5月1日在上述日期举行的群众大会。4月30日下午，大量盖有协会印章的小册子由卡特路伊园里15号总部的特派信使带到松茂里28号的东区分会办公室。共有四种不同种类的传单和一幅漫画。5月1日上午7时30分，几名成员来到松茂里的办公室，拿走成捆的传单。随后我们都按约定前往韬朋路。我们到达那里后不久，警察赶到，持有传单的人将传单扔在地上逃跑了。我只看到盖有“民众自救会抵制侮辱”印章的传单。我没有看到任何共产主义传单，如果有，我也不知道它们是从哪里来的。我不是共产党员，也从未与共产党有任何联系。

（签名）郑耀基（Zung Yoh Kyi）。

pages.en:
Loh Ching Foo (陸金虎).
Yienshin, Kiangsu,                                S.C.I. Forest
Yulin Rd. St.          1/5/33                     Clerk Jung Loon, Jan.

My name is Loh Ching Foo (陸金虎), I am 24 and a
native of Yienshin (宜興), Kiangsu. I attended school for
about one year at my native place and I can both read and write
Chinese. I came to Shanghai about three years ago and obtained
work as a coolie at the Dah Tung (大同) University, Nantao.
About 6 months later I left this position and obtained work as
an oiler at the King On Cotton Mill, Woosung, where I remained
until the commencement of the Sino-Japanese war in January,
1932. For the past year I have been employed as an oiler
at the Sung Sing No.9 Mill, Yangtszepoo Road. My parents came
to Shanghai from Yienshing about two years ago and took up
residence at No.52 Ying Zung Li (依仁里), Yangtszepoo Road,
and I have resided with them since I began work at the Sung
Sing Mill.

I am not a communist and have no connection with that party
but I am a member of the People's Self Salvation Association
to resist insult. I joined this association two weeks ago.
I was induced to join by a fellow worker named Pan Ah Deo (班阿大),
who took me to the office of the society at No.28 Seong Seu Li
(松茂里), Sangpan Road. I did not attend any meetings but
at 6 a.m. today (May 1) as I was going off night duty at the
mill I was met by the leader Kwei Tsang Yoeng (管正榮), who is
the Chief of the Organisation Department of the Eastern Branch
of the People's Self Salvation Association, to be on Tharburn
at 8 a.m. for the purpose of proceeding to the Public Recreation
Ground at the West Gate to stage demonstrations and to recruit
volunteers for the North Eastern Volunteer Army. I proceeded
pages.zh:
陆金虎（Loh Ching Foo）。
江苏宜兴（Yienshin），                                特别刑侦员 Forest
榆林路捕房          1933年5月1日                     朱伦（Jung Loon）书记员，一月。

我叫陆金虎（Loh Ching Foo），24岁，江苏宜兴人。我在家乡上学约一年，能读写中文。我大约三年前来到上海，在南市大同大学找到一份苦力的工作。大约6个月后，我离开了这个职位，在吴淞永安棉纺厂找到一份加油工的工作，一直干到1932年1月中日战争爆发。过去一年，我一直在杨树浦路的崇信九厂（Sung Sing No.9 Mill）担任加油工。我的父母大约两年前从宜兴来到上海，居住在杨树浦路依仁里52号，自从我开始在崇信厂工作以来，我一直与他们住在一起。

我不是共产党员，与该党没有任何联系，但我是“民众自救会抵制侮辱”的会员。我是两周前加入该协会的。我是被一名名叫班阿大（Pan Ah Deo）的同事诱导加入的，他带我去了宋潘路松茂里28号的协会办公室。我没有参加任何会议，但在今天（5月1日）上午6时，当我下班离开工厂时，遇到了领导人管正荣（Kwei Tsang Yoeng），他是民众自救会东区分会组织部部长，他让我在上午8时到韬朋路集合，目的是前往西门公共游乐场进行示威，并为东北义勇军招募志愿者。我 proceeded（原文未完）

pages.en:
Loh Ching Foo (陸全虎) - page 2.

to Thorburn Road at 8 a.m. and was there given a bundle of
handbills by Kwei Tsung Yoong (桂宗榮) which he told me to
distribute when we reached the West Gate. I opened the bundle
of handbills and found they contained appeals to the public
to support the People's Self Salvation Association to resist
insult. They were all of one kind and were not communist in
nature. Shortly afterwards the police arrived and we began
to run away but I was arrested together with Kwei Tsung Yoong
and several others. I was holding the bundle of handbills
when I was arrested but I at no time distributed any of them.
Kwei Tsung Yoong was the leader of the whole movement
and was in charge of the meeting.

(Signed) Loh Ching Foo.
pages.zh:
陆全虎（Loh Ching Foo）- 第2页。

上午8时前往陶尔白路（Thorburn Road），桂宗荣（Kwei Tsung Yoong）在那里交给我一捆传单，并告诉我当我们到达西门时分发这些传单。我打开这捆传单，发现其中内容是呼吁公众支持救国会以抵抗侮辱。这些传单均属同一类，不具有共产主义性质。不久后警察赶到，我们开始逃跑，但我与桂宗荣及其他几人一同被捕。被捕时我手中拿着那捆传单，但我从未分发过任何一张。桂宗荣是整个运动的领导人，并负责主持此次集会。

（签名）陆全虎。

pages.en:
Seized at 8.50 a.m. May 1 1933, by Yulin Road Station
at Wayside and Thorburn Road corner.

A handbill entitled
1. "A manifesto in connection with the urgent meeting 400 copies
to be held for the purpose of opposing the invasion
of North China by the Japanese imperialism m" bearing
the chop of the Propaganda Department of the
Western Branch of the National Salvation Association
to Resist Insult and denouncing the Government
for doing everything contrary to the wishes of the
people.

2. A handbill entitled "Circular telegram" and bearing 250 copies.
the chop of the Propaganda Department of the
Western Branch of the national Salvation Association
to Resist insult. Besides urging various public
organizations to pay attention to the present
national crisis this leaflet asks the people to
participate in the mass meeting to be held on
May 1st.

3. A handbill entitled "Manifesto issued for the 100 copies.
purpose of summoning Shanghai Eastern District
people to participate in the urgent meeting",
purporting to emanate from the Eastern Branch
of the National Salvation Association to
Resist insult, and denouncing the Government
for adopting the non-resistance policy.

4. A pamphlet bearing the slogans "Participate 15 copies.
in the Urgent Mass Meeting to be held at 1 p.m.
May 1st on public recreation ground in Nantao",
"Oppose the invasion of North China by Japan"
and "commemorate the warriors who sacrificed
their lives in the anti-Japanese campaign" and
dropped "Propaganda Department of the Eastern
Branch of the National Salvation Association
to Resist Insult.

5. A handbill purporting to emanate from the 30 copies.
Eastern Branch of the National Salvation
Association to Resist insult and urging the
toiling masses to attend the Urgent Mass
Meeting on May 1st for the purpose of protesting
against the non-resistance of the Government.

6. A handbill bearing the chop of the Eastern 200 copies.
Branch of the same Association (aforementioned)
urging people to attend the mass meeting and
stage anti-Japanese demonstration to commemorate
May 1st.

7. A pictorial entitled "Resist insult Pictorial", 20 copies.
purporting to emanate from the Self Salvation
Association to Resist insult, and containing
three cartoons one of which depicts four
persons shouting and bears the Chinese
characters "North China will be ruined, we
should convene urgent mass meeting and stage
demonstration to oppose the Japanese imperialism.

8. A handbill entitled "Letter to youth 20 copies.
workers of cotton mills" and urging the youth
workers of the cotton mills to demand freedom
of speech, publication and assembly.

1933年5月1日上午8时50分，由玉林路站（Yulin Road Station）在韦思德路（Wayside）与陶尔白路（Thorburn Road）拐角处查获。

一份题为
1. “关于为反对日本帝国主义侵略华北而召开紧急集会的宣言”的传单，共400份，盖有“救国会西分部宣传部”印章，谴责政府所做的一切违背人民意愿。

2. 一份题为“通电”的传单，共250份，盖有“救国会西分部宣传部”印章。除敦促各公共团体关注当前民族危机外，该传单还呼吁民众参加将于5月1日举行的群众大会。

3. 一份题为“为召集上海东区民众参加紧急集会而发布的宣言”的传单，共100份，声称出自“救国会东分部”，谴责政府采取不抵抗政策。

4. 一本小册子，印有标语“参加5月1日下午1时在南市公共游乐场举行的紧急群众大会”、“反对日本侵略华北”以及“纪念在抗日战役中牺牲的战士”，落款为“救国会东分部宣传部”。共15份。

5. 一份传单，声称出自“救国会东分部”，敦促劳苦大众参加5月1日的紧急群众大会，以抗议政府的不抵抗政策。共30份。

6. 一份传单，盖有上述同一协会（即前文所述）东分部的印章，敦促民众参加群众大会并举行反日游行以纪念五一节。共200份。

7. 一份题为“抗辱画报”的图画刊物，声称出自“救国自救会”，包含三幅漫画，其中一幅描绘四人呼喊，并配有汉字“华北危矣，吾人应开紧急群众大会及游行以反对日本帝国主义”。共20份。

8. 一份题为“致纱厂青年工人书”的传单，敦促纱厂青年工人要求言论、出版和集会自由。共20份。

"seized at 1.30 a.m. May 1, 1933, by Tulin [?] Station
at Sycia and Thorburn Road corner.

1) pamphlet entitled "Letter to Soldiers," ... 500 copies
from the ... of the Chinese Communist Youth
Group in connection with the May 1 Festival"
dated April 30, and consisting of the following
slogans :
Establish Soviet Government !
Long Live the Chinese Communistic Youths Group !
Oppose the attack on Soviet Union by the Imperialists !

2) A leaflet entitled "Greeting the Soviet Ambassador
to China" dated April 30 purporting to emanate from ...
the Kiangsu Provincial Committee of the Chinese
Communist Youths Group.

3) A pamphlet entitled "A Letter to Labourers, Students
and Toiling Masses throughout the Country in
connection with the Invasion of China by the
Japanese Imperialists" dated March 3, 1933 and
purporting to emanate from the Chinese Communist Party
and the Communist Youths Group. It calls upon
the Chinese to overthrow the Kuomintang and the
Imperialists and to establish Soviet.

4) A handbill entitled "A Manifesto of the Chinese
Provisional Soviet Government" dated March 4, 1933
and bearing the names of the President "Mao Tih
Tung" and the Vice Presidents "Wong Ming" and
"Chang Kuotao".

5) A leaflet entitled "A Letter to Calling Youths ... copies
to commemorate the April 12 Anniversary" and
purporting to emanate from the Yangtsepoo District
Committee of the Chinese Communist Party. It
contains usual communistic slogans.

6) A leaflet entitled "The Story of May 1" and concluded
by the usual communist slogans. 100 copies.

7) Two paper slips bearing the slogan "Down with the
'running' dog Kuomintang which kills and oppresses
upon the anti-Japanese people."

8) 20 paper slips bearing the slogan "Declare a strike
to commemorate the International Labour Day, May 1."

9) A leaflet purporting to emanate from the Kiangsu 100 copies
Provincial Committee of the Chinese Communist Youths
Group and bearing 16 slogans (the following are some
of them)
Support the red army to despatch soldiers to resist
the Japanese.
Down with the Kuomintang which prevents the red
army from despatching soldiers to resist the
Japanese.
Oppose the invasion of Soviet Russia by the Imperialists
as well as the attack on China.

10) A leaflet entitled "A Letter to Youth Labourers 200
in connection with the May 1 Festival" and purporting copies
to emanate Kiangsu Provincial Committee of the
Chinese Youths Group. This leaflet is dated
April 30.

“1933年5月1日凌晨1时30分，由图林[?]站（Tulin [?] Station）在西克西亚路（Sycia）与陶尔白路（Thorburn Road）拐角处查获。

1) 一本题为《致士兵书》的小册子，……共500份
来自……中国共产主义青年团，关于五一节事宜”，
日期为4月30日，包含以下标语：
建立苏维埃政府！
中国共产主义青年团万岁！
反对帝国主义者进攻苏联！

2) 一份题为《欢迎苏联驻华大使》的传单，日期为4月30日，声称出自……中国共产党江苏省委员会。

3) 一本题为《就日本帝国主义侵略中国事致全国劳工、学生及劳苦大众书》的小册子，日期为1933年3月3日，声称出自中国共产党和共产主义青年团。它号召中国人推翻国民党和帝国主义者，并建立苏维埃。

5) 一份题为《致青年……纪念四一二周年书》的传单，……份，声称出自中国共产党杨树浦区委。包含常见的共产主义标语。

6) 一份题为《五一故事》的传单，结尾为常见的共产主义标语。共100份。

8) 20张纸条，印有标语“宣布罢工以纪念国际劳动节五一。”

9) 一份传单，声称出自中国共产党江苏省委员会，印有16条标语（以下为部分标语）    共100份
支持红军派兵抗日。
打倒阻止红军派兵抗日的国民党。
